about: Open-source and DIY hardware that could take over an operation a setup leaves to a person or to a bought workcell device (#76). These are leads, never capabilities: nothing here changes a ranking, a fact or a person's equipment answers. Every entry cites its primary source (repository or paper; links checked 5 Nov 2026). 'platforms' lists the catalogue liquid handlers an entry attaches to, 'any' for a standalone device or software usable beside any setup, and 'standalone' for a complete open machine that replaces a liquid handler (shown in the catalogue only). Stated costs are the authors' own historical figures, not quotes. Maturity: 'peer-reviewed' (a paper describes the build and tests it), 'published design' (files released; no performance study found), 'prototype' (authors say incomplete or unvalidated, or archived), 'example code' (integration or driver code). An entry with a 'build' record can be modelled on its handler as a module the lab would build (#78): its capability values are the authors' reports, its labware fit is unknown unless a source settles it, and every fact it adds is a question until the builder confirms it.

maturity.peer-reviewed: A paper describes the build and reports tests.
maturity.published design: Design files or code are released; no performance study found.
maturity.prototype: Incomplete, archived, or stated by its authors as not yet validated.
maturity.example code: Integration or driver code, not hardware.

entries.name: Superior Magnet upgrade for the OT-2 Magnetic Module
entries.does: Replaces the stock magnet geometry with an Alpaqua 96S Super Magnet on a printed adapter and riser. The authors' motivation is poor bead pelleting, bead pickup and inconsistent supernatant removal with the stock side-pellet magnet in SPRI-style cleanups.
entries.limits: OT-2 Magnetic Modules are not Flex-compatible. Engage heights and labware definitions change with the adapter.
validate: Bead loss and residual volume against the stock magnet
Engage height and collision check with the chosen plate

build.requires: An OT-2 Magnetic Module to modify (GEN1 or GEN2) and an Alpaqua 96S Super Magnet.
build.basis: README: replaces the stock side-pellet magnet with the spring-loaded Alpaqua 96S Super Magnet on a printed adaptor and microplate riser.

entries.name: Indexed centrifuge for the OT-2

sources.title: Gao et al., Journal of Open Hardware 2024

entries.does: A centrifuge the OT-2 can reach, with automatic rotor indexing so the pipette can load and unload tubes. CAD, firmware and BOM are published.
entries.limits: Reported tube capacity is 1 mL; runs at ambient temperature, so no cold spins. A routine lab version needs a rated rotor, containment, balancing and lid/zero-speed interlocks.
validate: Containment and interlocks before routine use
Pellet recovery at the protocol's speed and volume
Whether ambient spins are acceptable for the step

build.requires: Printed rotor and structures, Arduino controller and parts from the published bill of materials.
build.basis: Gao et al. 2024 and repository: an indexed tube centrifuge the OT-2 pipette loads; reported tube capacity 1 mL, ambient temperature.

plate-96-pcr.detail: Tube rotor; plates are not spun (reported tube capacity 1 mL).

plate-96-deep.detail: Tube rotor; plates are not spun.

plate-384-pcr.detail: Tube rotor; plates are not spun.

entries.name: Claw-with-OT-2 gantry gripper
entries.does: An open gripper that bolts to the OT-2 gantry, so the robot can move plates between deck positions (for example on and off a magnet) without a person.
entries.limits: Loaded-plate grip, clearance and repeatability are not reported here.
validate: Loaded-plate moves between the positions the protocol uses
No collision with modules or tip racks

build.requires: Printed parts, two servos and the controller in the published bill of materials; the OT-2 front cover is removed to fit it.
build.basis: Assembly guide: a plate handler that slides onto the OT-2 gantry rails, with servo-driven vertical and horizontal movement.

entries.name: OpenSampler nanolitre syringe head on a modified OT-2

sources.title: OpenSampler paper, Journal of Separation Science

entries.does: Replaces the OT-2 pipette with a custom nanolitre syringe head, 3D-printed parts and its own control software (in place of the Opentrons Raspberry Pi stack). The closest published custom pipette on an OT-2.
entries.limits: Single channel. Bypasses the Opentrons software, so standard Opentrons protocols do not run unchanged.
validate: Gravimetric accuracy at the volumes the protocol needs
Carryover between samples

entries.name: Printed tip racks, tube racks and ice block for the OT-2
entries.does: STL files and custom labware definitions for racks that take cheaper TipOne-compatible tips, tube racks, an ice block for passive cold holds, and plate definitions.
entries.limits: The ice block is passive cold with no temperature control. The authors warn that official tips and racks are more reliable; printed tip racks suit short supervised runs, not unattended high-stakes ones. Opentrons quote terms may make non-Opentrons tips void the warranty.
validate: Block stays cold for the whole time reagents sit on deck (about 90 min reported)
No water leak through the printed PLA after repeated freeze-thaw
Tip pickup reliability over a full rack

build.requires: A printed holder, a StarLab mini dry-bath metal block and a -20 °C freezer.
build.basis: README: frozen overnight at -20 °C, the metal block stays around -10 °C for the first 30 min and around 0 °C for about another hour. Fits the OT-2 slot; not functionally verified.

entries.name: Printed tube racks and magnetic-module tube racks
entries.does: STL files for 0.5 and 1.5 mL tube racks, tube racks that sit on the Magnetic Module, an aluminium-block skirt and a syringe holder, so tube protocols can run on deck.
entries.limits: Magnetic pull through a printed tube rack differs from a plate on the module.
validate: Bead pelleting time in the tube rack on the magnet

entries.name: Microscope and plate-reader add-on for the OT-2
entries.does: A printed and off-the-shelf microscope / plate-reader style add-on built from Arduino, ESP32, GRBL and Raspberry Pi parts.
entries.limits: An engineering project, not a vendor-supported module; no quantitative reading performance found.
validate: Read-out against a reference instrument

entries.name: Opentrons integration examples (serial devices, cameras, robot arm)
entries.does: Opentrons' own examples for the HTTP API, serial devices, USB cameras, a QInstruments BioShake and a uFactory xArm moving plates to and from the robot. The pattern: describe the third-party device as labware so the robot avoids it, and control it from Python inside or beside the protocol.
entries.limits: Examples, not supported products; the arm and shaker are bought hardware.
validate: Collision geometry of each added device
Hand-off timing between robot and device

entries.name: Printed 96-well plate gripper for an SO-101 arm
entries.does: A replacement gripper for a low-cost SO-101 arm, using a bought linear rail and printed parts, to move plates between a liquid handler and bench stations.
entries.limits: Loaded-plate acceptance not assessed. Hobby servos need rigid nests, tapered guides and hard stops to place plates reliably.
validate: Loaded-plate approach, grip and release at every station
Pipetting alignment after a hand-off

entries.name: LeSlider arm rail
entries.does: An open linear rail that carries a low-cost arm along a bench to reach more stations.
entries.limits: Extends reach only; it does not make an arm that cannot reach into the deck usable.
validate: Positional repeatability at each station

entries.name: Scripps DIYbio orbital shaker
entries.does: CAD and controls for an open orbital plate shaker.
entries.limits: No heating or cooling; adding heat makes it a new, unvalidated design.
validate: Orbit and speed under load
Plate clamping

entries.name: OpenHW3 heated shaking apparatus
entries.does: A heated shaking apparatus reported for 25–75 °C.
entries.limits: Built for a different application; not a cooled block, so no 4 °C shaking.
validate: Liquid temperature in the protocol's plate
Shaking under load

entries.name: Open Temperature Block
entries.does: An open temperature-controlled block design.
entries.limits: Performance unproven for plate protocols.
validate: Temperature range, uniformity and ramp in the protocol's labware

entries.name: NinjaPCR
entries.does: An open PCR thermocycler project.
entries.limits: Not a 96-well plate cycler a robot can load; no heated auto-lid.
validate: Ramp rates and block uniformity against a commercial cycler

entries.name: Standalone control of the Opentrons Temperature Module
entries.does: Runs an Opentrons Temperature Module from an ordinary computer, without the robot. A used module can then serve as a cold or warm station beside any setup.
entries.limits: Needs a bought Temperature Module; plates still move by hand or by arm.
validate: Sample temperature in the protocol's labware

entries.name: Standalone control of the Opentrons Thermocycler

sources.title: HelixCycler: run the OT thermocycler independently of the robot

entries.does: Two projects that run an Opentrons Thermocycler from a computer without the robot, so a used cycler can work beside any setup.
entries.limits: Needs a bought Opentrons Thermocycler of a compatible generation.
validate: Programme timing and lid control match the protocol

entries.name: Opentrons OT-2 hardware files and module firmware
entries.does: Opentrons' own PCB files, wiring and pin-outs, deck drawings and dimensions for custom hardware, and firmware for the Temperature, Magnetic, Thermocycler and Heater-Shaker modules. The starting point for any custom add-on.
entries.limits: Reference material, not a device.

entries.name: Science Jubilee OT-2 pipette tool
entries.does: Mount, flexure and wiring to drive a real OT-2 pipette on an open Jubilee tool-changing machine, with tip pickup and ejection.
entries.limits: Documented with the single-channel P20 (1–20 µL); needs a bought pipette.
validate: Gravimetric accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: PANDA: an OT-2 pipette driven by an Arduino
entries.does: Drives an OT-2 pipette from an Arduino and a stepper driver on another machine.
entries.limits: The authors say it is not yet hardware-validated.
validate: Gravimetric accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: FINDUS pipetting robot
entries.statedCost: Under US$400 robot material (authors, historical; donor pipette extra)
entries.does: An open robot that motorises conventional hand pipettes, with automatic tip changing. Calibrated with P200 and P1000 over 20–1000 µL; at 20 µL the reported P200 errors are 0.610% systematic and 0.309% random.
entries.limits: Single channel as released; eight-channel use is discussed only as an extension.
validate: Accuracy at volumes below 20 µL if needed

entries.name: OTTO open liquid handler
entries.does: A complete open Cartesian robot that pushes a manual pipette; the paper reports qPCR set-up and a 5 µL single-channel dye test with 2.5% average error.
entries.limits: Single channel; no eight-channel performance.
validate: Accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: Opentrons OT-One open hardware
entries.does: Opentrons' 2015 open-hardware robot (Apache-2.0): CAD and BOM for a motor that presses a standard hand pipette, with an official eight-channel API.
entries.limits: Legacy software; current parts and price unresolved.
validate: Accuracy of the donor pipette on the rebuilt gantry

entries.name: USB driver for DLAB dPette electronic pipettes
entries.does: Serial control of volume, speed and mode on a DLAB electronic pipette, including the eight-channel. Mounted on an open gantry, this avoids building a motorised plunger.
entries.limits: Hardware logs cover 30–300 µL; no low-volume gravimetric test found. The driver's defaults allow 1000 µL, so the donor model's range must be enforced.
validate: Command compatibility with the exact pipette model
All-channel accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: 3D-printer pipetting robot
entries.does: Gantry code, mounts and plate-fill examples on a converted 3D printer, with working tip-rack pickup and fixed-bar tip ejection.
entries.limits: Archived prototype with manual coordinate calibration and no volumetric acceptance data.
validate: Accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: Ender 3 syringe liquid handler
entries.does: Marlin firmware, a web interface and syringe, plate and reservoir fixtures that turn an Ender 3 printer into a syringe dispenser.
entries.limits: The README claims about ±10 µL repeatability; not independently measured.
validate: Accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: Low-cost Jubilee pipette drive
entries.does: A cost-reduced pipette drive for the Jubilee with tip ejection, adapted from an earlier design.
entries.limits: No precision study found.
validate: Gravimetric accuracy

entries.name: 96-channel syringe pipette
entries.does: 96 syringes driven by four steppers, with CAD, firmware and build notes.
entries.limits: Hobby grade; no accuracy validation or robot integration.
validate: Per-channel accuracy

entries.name: Printed ISO 8655 four-channel pipette
entries.does: A manual printed four-channel 200 µL pipette reported as ISO 8655 compliant; a starting point for a motorised multichannel head.
entries.limits: Manual and four-channel.

entries.name: Open Lab Automata
entries.does: A documented open robot with tool changing, adapters and a protocol interface; its micropipette takes P20, P200 and P1000 tips (2–1000 µL).
entries.limits: Single channel; beta maturity.
validate: Accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: Sidekick dispenser
entries.does: A printed dispenser with solenoid pumps for adding reagents to plates.
entries.limits: Dispenses only; cannot aspirate.
validate: Dispense accuracy for each reagent's viscosity

entries.name: BioCloneBot
entries.does: A stepper-driven Hamilton syringe head on an Ender 3 frame, presented as a low-cost alternative to an OT-2.
entries.limits: Single channel.
validate: Accuracy at the protocol's volumes

entries.name: HelixCycler: standalone control of the Opentrons Thermocycler
entries.does: A Python application that runs an Opentrons Thermocycler without the robot. A loose or used module can then work as a bench cycler beside any setup.
entries.limits: Needs a bought Opentrons Thermocycler. The README does not say which module generations it supports. Plates are loaded by hand or by an arm.
validate: Which Thermocycler generation the lab's module is, and whether the app drives it
Block and lid temperatures in the protocol's plates

entries.name: SO-101 autosyringe end effector and plate light table
entries.does: A printed end effector that turns a low-cost SO-101 arm into a syringe dispenser. The arm's gripper servo drives a 10 mL syringe, and a 96-well plate sits on a USB light table. STLs cover the body, rack, gear, plunger holder, camera mount and plate holder.
entries.limits: A 10 mL syringe with no reported accuracy. There are no disposable tips, so carryover between wells or reagents is uncontrolled. The stock arm and servo are donor hardware.
validate: Dispense accuracy at the protocol's volumes
Carryover between reagents

entries.name: Seeed B601-DM arm with camera mounts, gripper fingers and bed fixtures
entries.does: Calibration and demonstration code, OAK camera mounts, gripper fingers and pads, and printer-bed fixtures for a low-cost Seeed B601-DM arm, aimed at camera-guided plate handling.
entries.limits: The authors state that plate pickup is not commissioned. They also report an incident in which the arm knocked a plate out.
validate: Loaded-plate pickup and placement at each station
Collision-free approach after any change to the bed

entries.name: BioKEA xArm 7 plate shuttle
entries.does: Workflow code for a stock uFactory xArm 7 that moves a 96-well plate between a picking station and an imager or plate-reader station.
entries.limits: A hackathon artifact. The arm is bought hardware, and the payload settings are still placeholders.
validate: Loaded-plate transfer at working speed after the payload values are set
Hand-off positions at each station
